title: Finite-free total tensor model with degree bounds
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $F^\bullet,G^\bullet$ be cochain complexes of $R$-modules, and let $c,d\in\mathbf Z$. Suppose every term is finite free (has a finite basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]), $F^p=0$ for $p>c$, and $G^q=0$ for $q>d$. Write $\mathsf Q$ for localization into $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and form the direct-sum total tensor complex
$$E^\bullet=\operatorname{Tot}(F^\bullet\otimes_R G^\bullet),\qquad E^k=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}F^p\otimes_R G^q,$$
with differential $d(x\otimes y)=d_Fx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes d_Gy$ for $x\in F^p$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Then $E^k$ is finite free for every integer $k$, and $E^k=0$ for $k>c+d$. More precisely, for finite bases $(f_{p,i})_{i\in I_p}$ of $F^p$ and $(g_{q,j})_{j\in J_q}$ of $G^q$, the summand inclusions of the vectors $f_{p,i}\otimes g_{k-p,j}$, indexed by the finite set $\coprod_{k-d\le p\le c}(I_p\times J_{k-p})$, form a basis of $E^k$. The complexes $F^\bullet,G^\bullet,E^\bullet$ are K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], and there is a natural isomorphism
$$\mathsf Q(E^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf Q(F^\bullet)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\mathsf Q(G^\bullet)$$
for the K-flat derived tensor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], given by its K-flat comparison. If also $F^p=0$ for $p<e$ and $G^q=0$ for $q<f$, where $e,f\in\mathbf Z$, then $E^k=0$ for $k<e+f$; in particular bounded inputs give a bounded finite-free total complex.

proof.text: Use the direct-sum totalization of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], specialized to modules on the one-point site. In degree $k$, write $q=k-p$. If $p>c$ the first factor is zero, and if $p<k-d$ the second factor is zero. A tensor with a zero module is zero because it is generated by pure tensors, all zero. Thus only the finite integer interval $k-d\le p\le c$ contributes. For $k>c+d$ this interval is empty, so $E^k=0$.

source.place: Tag 0DJE, lemma-tensor-pseudo-coherent, displayed total tensor; degree-support calculation

proof.text: For every remaining $p$, [lem-sc-tensor-product-free-basis] gives the basis $f_{p,i}\otimes g_{k-p,j}$ of $F^p\otimes_R G^{k-p}$. Every element of $E^k$ is a tuple of elements of these summands, and expanding each coordinate in that basis expresses it in the asserted included vectors. If a linear combination of these vectors is zero, projection onto the $p$-summand and uniqueness in its tensor basis force all its coefficients to vanish. These vectors therefore form a basis in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. The indexing set is finite: there are finitely many integers in the interval and each $I_p\times J_{k-p}$ is finite. Hence $E^k$ is finite free.

proof.text: The hypotheses give finite-free terms for $F,G$, and step 2 gives them for $E$. Apply [lem-sc-affine-standard-cover-finite-free-local-fp-flat] to each term to get flatness. The three complexes vanish above $c,d,c+d$, respectively. Therefore [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] applies separately to each and gives K-flatness. Its acyclic-total-tensor criterion is exactly the module K-flatness of [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]; no boundedness below or Noetherian hypothesis is used.

proof.text: In [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] put $A=R$, $N=G$, and use the identity K-flat resolution $F\xrightarrow{1}F$. Clause (2) identifies $\mathsf Q(F)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\mathsf Q(G)$ with $\mathsf Q(\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_R G))=\mathsf Q(E)$. Invert that canonical comparison to get the displayed direction. It is natural in $F$ by the functorial derived comparison of (2), and in $G$ by (3), which represents a cochain map $u:G\to G^{\prime}$ by $\operatorname{Tot}(1_F\otimes u)$. Thus the isomorphism is the K-flat comparison, independently of the bases used to prove termwise freeness.

source.place: Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change and preceding K-flat construction, applied to the identity ring map

proof.text: Under the additional lower bounds, a summand in degree $k$ can be nonzero only when $p\ge e$ and $q\ge f$. For $k=p+q<e+f$ these inequalities cannot both hold. All summands of the direct-sum totalization [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] are then zero, so $E^k=0$. Together with the upper bound and step 2 this proves that bounded inputs give a bounded finite-free total complex.
